Directed Erdos-Renyi graphs yield the bound $O_P(λ_N^{-1/2}+\|π_N-π\|_1)$ when $λ_N\to\infty$ and $λ_N/N\to0$. This separates stable averaging at a fixed delay from singular collapse. In the latter, componentwise weak convergence discards signed arrival-order information needed by the threshold-reset response.

AI.tldr: Componentwise weak convergence of synaptic kernels is insufficient to determine the fast-synapse limit in sparse threshold-reset networks. The paper constructs two network families with identical excitatory/inhibitory measures converging weakly to δ₀ but reversed microscopic arrival orders, producing opposite firing outcomes for targets with x+a-b<θ≤x+a. The discrepancy persists macroscopically on moderately sparse random graphs, differing in population-averaged firing counts by 1/2+o_{L1}(1) along every deterministic scale ε_N↓0, and is robust to perturbations. Stable regimes exist for fixed positive-delay kernels with finitely many classes, where typewise-mixing sparse networks converge to delayed class mean-field systems.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that weak convergence of synaptic kernel measures is insufficient to characterize the fast-synapse limit of sparse threshold-reset networks, because componentwise weak convergence discards signed arrival-order information that critically affects the threshold-reset response.
AI.method: Constructs two network families with reversed microscopic arrival orders while maintaining identical weakly-converging E/I measures, using a causal event protocol with clamped refractoriness and smooth positive-delay kernels. Analyzes firing responses under perturbations, extends to moderately sparse Dale-compatible random block graphs and directed Erdos-Renyi graphs, and develops a stable regime for fixed positive-delay kernels with finitely many classes via typewise-mixing sparse networks.
AI.result: A target fires in the excitatory-first family but not the inhibitory-first family exactly when x+a-b<θ≤x+a. Population-averaged firing counts differ by 1/2+o_{L1}(1) along every deterministic joint scale. Directed Erdos-Renyi graphs yield bound O_P(λ_N^{-1/2}+‖π_N-π‖_1) when λ_N→∞ and λ_N/N→0, separating stable averaging at fixed delay from singular collapse.
AI.conclusion: Componentwise weak convergence alone fails to determine fast-synapse limits in sparse threshold-reset networks; signed arrival-order information is essential. Stable averaging occurs for fixed-delay typewise-mixing networks, but singular collapse requires additional structure beyond componentwise weak convergence.

title: Unsupervised Learning of Cell Instances with Generative Routing Pyramids
summary: Identifying and representing object instances such as cells or nuclei is a common task in microscopy image analysis. Established machine learning workflows typically use supervised detection or segmentation followed by feature extraction or classification, which requires manual annotations and treats instance segmentation and cell representation as separate stages. We describe a new unsupervised method for cell instance segmentation and phenotypic classification from unlabeled microscopy images. Our method is based on reconstructing each image using a coarse-to-fine routing pyramid that associates pixels with spatially sparse latent sources. The resulting pixel-to-latent associations yield instance masks, while the source latents encode cell morphology. We demonstrate competitive performance in instance segmentation across diverse cell morphologies and imaging modalities, as well as generative modeling of cellular phenotypes under perturbations. Source code and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/weigertlab/routing-pyramids.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces an unsupervised method for cell instance segmentation and phenotypic classification in microscopy images using a coarse-to-fine routing pyramid that reconstructs images via sparse latent sources, yielding instance masks and morphological encodings without manual annotations.
AI.motivation: Traditional machine learning workflows for microscopy image analysis require manual annotations and treat instance segmentation and cell representation as separate stages, which is labor-intensive and fragmented. The authors aim to develop an unsupervised approach that jointly handles both tasks without labeled data.
AI.method: The method reconstructs each image using a coarse-to-fine routing pyramid that associates pixels with spatially sparse latent sources. Pixel-to-latent associations generate instance masks, while the latent sources themselves encode cell morphology for phenotypic classification.
AI.result: The method demonstrates competitive performance in instance segmentation across diverse cell morphologies and imaging modalities, and enables generative modeling of cellular phenotypes under perturbations. Source code and checkpoints are publicly available.
AI.conclusion: An unsupervised routing-pyramid-based approach can effectively perform both cell instance segmentation and phenotypic classification simultaneously, offering a viable alternative to supervised, annotation-dependent pipelines in microscopy analysis.

title: Complete characterization of the sign of the wave speed in the symmetric Lotka-Volterra system under strong competition
summary: This paper provides a complete characterization of the sign of the propagation speed in the symmetric two-species Lotka-Volterra competition-diffusion model under strong competition. The system admits a unique bistable travelling front and the sign of its speed determines which of the two species invades the other. We prove that for every strong competition intensity greater than $1$ and every diffusion ratio $d\neq1$, the travelling front propagates so as to expand the territory occupied by the faster-diffusing species. The front has a zero speed exactly when $d=1$. We also establish the smooth dependence of the wave speed and the travelling front on the model parameters. The main step in the sign characterization is to prove that a monotone standing front cannot exist when the diffusion rates are different. Combined with continuity of the wave speed with respect to the parameters, the species-exchange symmetry of the system, and an explicit travelling front at a particular parameter value, we obtain the sign of the propagation speed throughout the entire parameter region. This establishes the ``Unity is not strength'' theorem, which was previously known only in restricted parameter regimes.

AI.tldr: This paper fully characterizes the sign of the propagation speed in a symmetric two-species Lotka-Volterra competition-diffusion model under strong competition, proving that the travelling front always expands the territory of the faster-diffusing species when diffusion rates differ, with zero speed only when d=1.
AI.motivation: While the "Unity is not strength" theorem—that the faster-diffusing species invades—was previously known only in restricted parameter regimes, this work aims to provide a complete characterization of the sign of the propagation speed across the entire parameter region for strong competition.
AI.method: The main step is proving that a monotone standing front cannot exist when diffusion rates are different. Combined with continuity of the wave speed with respect to parameters, the species-exchange symmetry of the system, and an explicit travelling front at a particular parameter value, the authors obtain the sign of the propagation speed throughout the entire parameter region.

The front has zero speed exactly when d=1. The paper also establishes smooth dependence of wave speed and front on model parameters.
AI.conclusion: The paper establishes the "Unity is not strength" theorem in full generality, completing the sign characterization of the propagation speed that was previously known only in restricted parameter regimes.
